@atiratree Need some help again😂. I ran the tests in #119915 on this branch. And the test in #119915 is failing. It's because the rollbacked deployment has a `"kubernetes.io/pod-template-hash"` in it's `spec.template.labels`.
So I ran the tests locally, first I ran with kubectl version `v1.29.0-alpha.0.23` (with updated code), and everything works fine. Then I ran the tests with kubectl version `v1.28`, and yes, I reproduce the problem, the deployment will have a `"kubernetes.io/pod-template-hash"` in it's `spec.template.labels` after rolled back.
So, I have some questions:

1. Seems that when running kubectl tests in e2e, it doesn't use the kubectl built from current source code?
2. As this behavior is different with two different version of kubectl, I tend to think it's because we didn't delete new label in the old kubectl. This doesn't seem to satisfy compatibility?

it uses  kubectl from path by default. You can change it if you need to. 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f3d0392e073174921f6eba6f71fde6e3313142fc/test/e2e/framework/test_context.go#L359

> As this behavior is different with two different version of kubectl, I tend to think it's because we didn't delete new label in the old kubectl. This doesn't seem to satisfy compatibility?

hm you are right, it seems to me we have to support rollback for the last version of kubectl according to the skew policy: https://kubernetes.io/releases/version-skew-policy/. 

I am seeing two options.

- put the controller code behind a feature gate and put the change in the kubectl immediately 
- put the change in the kubectl immediately, but wait with the changes for the controller until the next release

I am more inclined to do the first option as it is more safe and k8s way of doing things. The second option would be faster.

> I am more inclined to do the first option as it is more safe and k8s way of doing things. The second option would be faster.

I prefer the first option too. I'll continue on this after #119915 merged :)

@atiratree I've added a new feature gate.

If we have to keep adding the `pod-template-hash` label (which I think we do for compatibility), it's not clear to me what the benefit of adding *another* label with the same value is. This seems like it only adds edge cases and potential problems:
* client decides to use the prefixed label and fails against older clusters
* the two labels get out of sync

Can't we put the old label into the deprecation process?
The good thing is that most users shouldn't be affected: new selectors will only use the new label.

It's only developers who explicitly depend on `pod-template-hash` that need to update their code.

> Can't we put the old label into the deprecation process?

If we did, it's not explicitly described as unstable, so my starting point would be to treat it as deprecating a stable thing. If there's strong reasons to do so, we can, but I don't see reasons that outweigh the effort to sweep and transition any uses of this.

> The good thing is that most users shouldn't be affected: new selectors will only use the new label.

How would we detect and ensure users weren't impacted?

> It's only developers who explicitly depend on `pod-template-hash` that need to update their code.

You're more optimistic than I am that all of those developers are paying attention to changes that would require them to modify that code :)

PR needs rebase.

issue_context.title: Pod template tracking uses fixed, non-prefixed label keys
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

Per https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114930#issuecomment-1469940664, the `pod-template-hash` label is a private one (reserved for cluster operators). It should be something more like `kubernetes.io/pod-template-hash` or maybe `kubernetes.io/pod-template-hash-sha256`.

### How can we reproduce it?

(for example)
Deploy a Kubernetes cluster that includes CoreDNS running as a Deployment.

/sig apps

https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/labels-annotations-taints/ lists all the registered label and annotation keys for the Kubernetes project.

review_comments:
actually, can we remove the old key from the selector?
This means that the RS selector for new RS is independent of the legacy label, but users can still use the legacy label for a bit, if they are not paying attention to the selector.

We only need to make sure that we wouldn't recreate a replicaset just because it doesn't have the new label.
I'm not fully familiar with deployment controller to see if these changes are enough. Do we need any changes in FindNewReplicaSet?

We did the same for the job controller https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114930
Updted. I think in `FindNewReplicaSet` we compare two rs without hash label, so it should be ok. But I'm not sure as I'm not familiar with deployment controller.

yes, we are not using the hashes for looking up/identifying the RSes, so it should be fine to use only the new label in the selector. The only potential problem I am seeing is, if somebody orphaned their pods and wanted to move them between replicasets while bringing this change in.
maybe we could also check the replica set here, that it has the correct labels and selector?
can we add `DeploymentUniqueLabelKey` into `TestFindNewReplicaSet` and `TestFindOldReplicaSets` tests to prepare these for future removal of `DefaultDeploymentUniqueLabelKey`?
